content: General Baby Care: Always wash your hands thoroughly before and after handling the baby. Do not share baby care supplies with other infants to prevent cross-contamination. Umbilical Cord Care: Wash your hands before and after caring for the umbilical cord. Do not apply any substances or bandages to the cord stump. Fold the diaper below the cord stump to keep it dry and clean. Ensure the cord stump is loosely covered with clean clothing. If the stump becomes soiled, clean it with clean water and soap, then dry it thoroughly with a clean cloth. If the umbilical area becomes red, or if there is pus or blood drainage, examine the baby and manage the condition appropriately. Advise the mother to seek medical care if these signs occur. Avoid unnecessary touching of the cord stump. Sleeping Guidelines: Use a bed net during both day and night to protect the baby while sleeping. Place the baby to sleep on their back or side. Keep the baby away from smoke or individuals who are smoking. Hygiene and Bathing: At birth, only remove blood or meconium. Do not remove the vernix (the white, waxy substance on the baby’s skin). Do not bathe the baby until they are at least 6 hours old. Later, at home, wash the baby’s face, neck, and underarms daily. Clean the buttocks when soiled and dry thoroughly. Bathe the baby only when necessary, ensuring the room is warm and free of drafts. Use warm water, dry the baby thoroughly, and dress them immediately after the bath. Other Baby Care: Use a clean cloth to collect the baby’s stool and dispose of it properly, similar to how a woman’s sanitary pads are disposed of. Do not bathe the baby if they are less than 6 hours old or if they are cold. Do not apply anything to the baby’s eyes except antimicrobial ointment at birth. Breastfeeding and Preventive Measures: Begin resuscitation within one minute of birth if the baby is not breathing or gasping for air. Keep the baby warm by clamping and cutting the cord, transferring them to a dry, clean, and warm surface, and wrapping them in a blanket. Use a radiant heater if available. Position the baby’s head slightly extended to open the airway. Use a folded towel under the shoulders if necessary. Suction the mouth and nose only if there are visible secretions, and avoid routine suctioning. If the baby is not breathing, use a mask to provide positive pressure ventilation. Ensure a proper seal and observe chest rise. Adjust the head position or mask seal if the chest does not rise. Ventilate at a rate of 40 squeezes per minute for one minute, then assess the heart rate. If the heart rate is above 100 beats per minute and the baby is breathing or crying, stop ventilating. Treatment and Immunization: Administer 1 mg of vitamin K intramuscularly to all newborns one hour after birth to prevent bleeding disorders. Provide intramuscular antibiotics (ampicillin and gentamicin) for babies with signs of serious infection or those at risk of infection. Teach the mother how to administer medications at home, ensuring she understands the instructions and can measure and give the correct dose. Local Infection Treatment: For skin pustules or umbilical infections, clean the area three times daily by washing hands, gently cleaning off pus and crusts with boiled and cooled water and soap, drying the area, and applying gentian violet. For eye infections, clean the eyes 6–8 times daily with boiled and cooled water, and apply 1% tetracycline eye ointment three times daily. Follow-Up and Danger Signs: Advise the mother to return for follow-up visits if the baby has feeding difficulties, red umbilicus, skin infections, or eye infections. Immediate medical attention is required for difficulty breathing, convulsions, fever, bleeding, diarrhea, or if the baby is not feeding at all. HIV-Exposed Newborns: Administer antiretroviral drugs (e.g., nevirapine and zidovudine) within 6–12 hours of birth. Teach the mother how to give these medications at home and ensure she understands the importance of daily administration for 6 weeks. Immunization: Administer BCG, OPV-0, and Hepatitis B vaccines within 24 hours of birth, preferably before discharge. Record the immunizations and advise the mother on when to return for the next doses. Laboratory Testing: For syphilis testing, perform a rapid plasma reagin (RPR) test by collecting a blood sample, separating the serum, and applying it to a test card with antigen. Interpret results based on clumping patterns. For HIV testing, follow national guidelines for rapid testing procedures. Transportation During Referral: Keep the baby warm during transportation by maintaining skin-to-skin contact with the mother or another caregiver. Cover the baby with a blanket and protect them from direct sunlight. Encourage breastfeeding during the journey.
